transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. No, it is not safe to use. You must unplug the microwave immediately and do not run it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. The blue flashes on the right-hand wall with crackling are classic signs of arcing, most likely caused by a burnt or holed waveguide cover (the small rectangular panel on the side wall) or food splatter that has carbonised into a conductive path. While you can safely check for any obvious metal items or heavy dirt inside when it is unplugged, do not attempt to repair the internal components yourself as they hold dangerous high-voltage charges even when disconnected.

candidates: Metal object or food debris inside cavity (medium)

reading.symptom: sparking inside, blue flashes on the right-hand wall, crackling noise

tags.checkGiven: With it unplugged and the door open, take out anything metal or foil, then look closely at the small flat cover panel on the inside wall (us

plan: They asked: "Is it safe?" - answer that first.

Safety: a microwave arcing hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Panasonic; model NN-ST45KWBPQ.
The fault they reported is: "sparking inside, blue flashes on the right-hand wall, crackling noise". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
